cohort: Newborns admitted to neonatal units at the University College Hospital, Ibadan, Nigeria and Jaramogi Oginga Odinga Teaching and Referral Hospital, Kisumu, Kenya.
finding: Gut colonisation by ESBL organisms was common (89% of infants) and occurred rapidly (median 7 days), while carbapenemase producers were also prevalent (62.4%) but colonisation occurred later (median 16 days) in neonates admitted to NNUs in Kenya and Nigeria.
